question: Do the OKX original-signal runner conclusions transfer when Binance's 2R limit has the identical twelve-hour validity as OKX, instead of its previously stored long-lived target?
single_variable: Change only the life of the existing native 2R order. Cancel unexecuted 2R children at entry plus 12h, before that next open. Preserve any earlier fill. Thereafter use the same child having the native fixed stop, adverse cloud exit and, where applicable, its unchanged absolute-doubling limit. Each comparison has its own already tested native lifetime control: (a) two-thirds 2R and half of surviving longs offered at 2x price, (b) one-third 2R and half offered on doubling, (c) two-thirds 2R and no doubling sale. Within each matched pair no other variable changes. Between the three aligned arms only compare (a) to (b) to assess 2R fraction or (a) to (c) to assess doubling sale.
source: Native 1583 Binance V1.7 confirmed 12H parent fills, fixed independent Binance queue and historical funding. A route check before testing showed 486 baseline native 2R targets versus 67 on the existing OKX wallet; 418 Binance exits occurred at/after 12 hours, zero on OKX. This is retrospective alignment after checking this discrepancy. Use the same nominal 2/5bp fee schedule, 10% of previous 60-minute median entry turnover and hourly 20% single-contract trim, separate adverse 5bp stress and both funding-clock boundary policies. Chronological comparison only; markets, queues, calendar coverage, exposures and funding coverage still differ by venue.
